author: claude
title: Don't Put All Your Eggs in One Basket

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: There is an old saying: don't put all your eggs in one basket. If you drop the basket, every egg breaks. In investing, this idea is called diversification.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Diversification means spreading your money across many different investments, so that one bad result does not destroy your savings. If you put everything into one company and that company fails, you could lose almost everything. If you own small pieces of hundreds of companies, one failure has only a small effect.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Diversification works best when investments do not all move together. Investors call this correlation. If two assets always rise and fall at the same time, holding both does not reduce risk very much. So investors spread money across different industries, different countries and different types of assets, such as stocks, bonds and sometimes real estate.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: For example, when the economy slows down, stock prices may fall, but some bonds may hold their value or even rise. When one area is weak, another may be stronger.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: However, diversification cannot remove all risk. During a global crisis, many assets can fall at the same time. This kind of market-wide risk is called systematic risk, and no amount of diversification can fully avoid it.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Still, diversification is one of the few things in investing that many experts call a free lunch. It can reduce risk without necessarily reducing your expected return. For most people, a low-cost, globally diversified fund is a simple way to achieve it.
